The limitation of large pre-trained models that motivates the use of retrieval is that they often store factual knowledge in their parameters, which can lead to overfitting and decreased performance when fine-tuning them on downstream NLP tasks, such as question answering.

In other words, large pre-trained language models have been shown to retain a significant amount of knowledge from their training data, which can be difficult to transfer to new tasks. This can result in poor performance when the model is fine-tuned on a new task, such as question answering, where the model needs to learn new relationships and concepts.

The use of retrieval modules, which are designed to retrieve relevant information from a large pre-trained model, can help to mitigate this limitation. By learning a retrieval module to augment the pre-trained model, researchers can leverage the strengths of both the pre-trained model and the retrieval module, leading to improved performance on downstream tasks.
